growth.note: The bound applies to every fixture measured at more than one size, and it is 1.25 because the cost per plan entry has to stay flat as the fleet grows: `fleet` grows the number of entries and keeps each entry's own work constant, `mesh` grows one entry's work with the fleet and keeps the plan linear in it, and a quarter of slack absorbs constant-factor noise without admitting any super-linear term.

worked.note: Re-recorded on the review that closed ten totality violations and the wildcard, reservation-key and root-account soundness holes. Two things moved these figures. The budgets had not been re-recorded since 2026-09-11, so eleven feature merges of accumulated cost are folded in at once: 58% of the overage this re-record absorbs predates the seven merges under review, which contributed 7.4% to 9.8% between them, and `type-a-port-claim-and-its-collision` was a net saving of 1.27 thunks per entry. The fixtures also now exercise what the features added: a second port claim of one number under a different address so the overlap comparison is entered, a machine reservation on every registry machine, a configuration file with a stated owner and group read by a unit that declares an account and a group, a per-entry runtime directory and one deliberately shared state directory. Against this a throw planted in `contends`, `opens`, `reservedBy`, `claimedUnder` or `collisionRow` fires, where before it never did and the gated figures measured the old deployment shape. Working the other way, gating the deep string walk on `util.anyLineBreak` returned 9.67 thunks per entry on fleet and 14.33 on mesh, which is most of the newest merge's cost.
